title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 122
paragraphs: As Cyrus grew to be a man, being of all those of his age the most courageous and the best beloved, Harpagos sought to become his friend and sent him gifts, because he desired to take vengeance on Astyages. For he could not see how, from his own private station, punishment should come upon Astyages; but when he saw Cyrus growing up, he tried to make him an ally, finding a likeness between Cyrus's fortunes and his own. Even before this he had done something: for since Astyages was harsh to the Medes, Harpagos communicated separately with the chief men of the Medes and persuaded them that they ought to make Cyrus their leader and cause Astyages to cease being king. When he had achieved this and all was ready, Harpagos, wishing to make his design known to Cyrus, who lived among the Persians, could do it no other way, since the roads were watched, and so devised this scheme: he prepared a hare, and having cut open its belly but without pulling off any of the fur, he placed inside it, just as it was, a piece of paper on which he had written what he thought good. Then he sewed up the belly of the hare again, and giving nets to the most trusted of his servants as if he were a hunter, he sent him to the land of the Persians, enjoining him by word of mouth to give the hare to Cyrus, and to tell him to open it with his own hands and let no one else be present when he did so.
